title: Flagsmith
name: flagsmith
description: Feature flags and remote config for your apps: switch features on per environment, roll out to a percentage or a segment of users, and change values without a deploy, with SDKs for most languages. Source: https://github.com/Flagsmith/flagsmith

env.name: FLAGSMITH_SECRET
env.label: Secret key (required)
env.description: Signs everyone's logins. Generate one with: openssl rand -hex 32. Keep it the same when you redeploy.

env.name: FLAGSMITH_DB_PASSWORD
env.label: Database password (required)
env.description: Generate one with: openssl rand -hex 32. Keep it the same when you redeploy, or Flagsmith can't reach its database.

env.name: FLAGSMITH_SECURE_COOKIES
env.label: Opening it over plain http?
env.description: Flagsmith only keeps you logged in over HTTPS unless this is on. Switch it off once it's behind a reverse proxy with HTTPS.

env.name: FLAGSMITH_PORT
env.label: Host port for the web UI and API

note: Fill in the secret key and database password before you deploy, since the stack won't start without them (openssl rand -hex 32 makes a good one of each), and keep both the same when you redeploy. The first start takes a minute or two while it builds the database. Then open it on port 8600 straight away and click Get Started, as whoever gets there first makes the admin account and the first organisation. The free self-hosted edition allows one project per organisation, so for another project click the logo at the top left, then Create Organisation. There's no email set up, so email invites and password resets won't send. Bring teammates in with the invite link under Users and Permissions instead. Anyone who can reach it can sign up too, so once your people are in, add FLAGSMITH_PREVENT_SIGNUP set to true to the stack's environment variables and redeploy (that closes the invite link as well). Point your apps' SDKs at http://<address>:8600/api/v1/. Everything lives in Postgres, in the postgres-data volume. Two things phone home. On every start the server sends Flagsmith a count of your organisations, projects, flags and users (add FLAGSMITH_TELEMETRY set to false to stop it). And the dashboard loads its own feature flags from Flagsmith's cloud, sending your user id, email and organisation name along with them. To keep that in-house, make an organisation just for this with one project in it, copy the client-side key from that project's SDK Keys page, then add FLAGSMITH_UI_FLAGS_KEY set to that key and FLAGSMITH_UI_FLAGS_URL set to /api/v1/, and redeploy. Docs: docs.flagsmith.com
